Connecting to a Breedbase instance

Source: R/breedbase_brapi.R
breedbase_connection.Rd

How to connect breedtools to a 'Breedbase' site, such as the production site https://cassavabase.org or the test site https://cassava-test.sgn.cornell.edu. Every function that reads from or writes to Breedbase takes the connection returned by breedbase_login() as its con argument.

What you need

  • The address of the site, e.g. "https://cassavabase.org". Any Breedbase site with BrAPI v2 works, for example other crop databases on the same software.

  • A user account on that site, created on the site itself ("Login" then "New user"). Accounts are separate for each site: an account on cassavabase.org does not exist on cassava-test, and the reverse.

  • To save trials, phenotypes or analyses, your account must be allowed to write to the breeding program (the site's curators grant this). Reading works with any account.

  • The 'httr2' package, and optionally 'askpass' for password pop-ups.

Production and test sites

A production site (e.g. cassavabase.org) holds the real data of the breeding programs: everything you save there is shared with them. A test site (e.g. cassava-test.sgn.cornell.edu) is a copy for trying things out; use it to learn the workflow or to try a new script before saving to production. Test sites also protect their web pages with an extra web password (the browser pop-up "Restricted Test Site"). BrAPI calls, used for trials, plots and phenotypes, do not need it; the trait composer and the upload of analyses do. Give it with site_username (and site_password or BREEDBASE_SITE_PASSWORD). Without it, the login first tries your Breedbase user name and password there and, in an interactive session, asks for the web password.

Passwords

Never write a password in a script. Either leave it empty and type it in the pop-up, or store it once in your personal ~/.Renviron file (open it with usethis::edit_r_environ()), then restart R:


BREEDBASE_PASSWORD=your_breedbase_password
BREEDBASE_SITE_PASSWORD=the_test_site_web_password

Scripts run without a console (Rscript, scheduled jobs) need these variables, since there is nobody to answer the pop-up. Only the access token is kept in the connection; the password is not stored.

Check the connection

Printing the connection shows the site, the user and whether a web password is set. List the programs, folders and locations to confirm that the account sees the data you expect, and use dry_run = TRUE in the save_*() functions to check everything without writing. When the token expires (a long session), log in again.

Working without a connection

Designs, analyses, prepare_breedbase_trial() and the dry runs of save_breedbase() work offline, so a whole design can be prepared before logging in.

See also

breedbase_login(), breedbase_lists, breedbase_check(), save_breedbase(), breedbase_phenotypes(), save_breedbase_analysis()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Production site
con <- breedbase_login("https://cassavabase.org", username = "your_username")
con
breedbase_programs(con)

# Test site, with its extra web password
test <- breedbase_login("https://cassava-test.sgn.cornell.edu",
                        username = "your_username",
                        site_username = "web_user_name")
breedbase_locations(test)
} # }
